result:
Admins can now change a user's role from a select in each row of the users table. I didn't run tests, lint or the app, so none of this has been exercised.

The select shows ADMIN or USER. Changing it sends `PATCH /users/{userId}/role` with `{ role }`. On success the users list is refetched, so the new role appears, and a "User Role Updated" notification is shown. The select is disabled for your own row, so an admin can't demote themself, and while a change is in flight.

**Where things are:**
- The API fetcher, input schema and mutation hook are in `features/users/api/update-user-role.ts`.
- The row select is in `features/users/components/update-user-role.tsx`, wired into the Role column of `users-list.tsx`.
- I added a mock handler for the endpoint in `testing/mocks/handlers/users.ts`. It requires an admin and only updates users in the caller's team.

**Lint rule:** the project's `no-restricted-imports` rule says success notifications belong in the api hook, not in feature components. I put the notification in the mutation hook to comply. The existing `delete-user.tsx` and `update-profile.tsx` still call `useNotifications` in their components and would presumably hit the same rule. I left them alone.

A hook error flagged the component's `useNotifications` import before I moved the notification. A text search shows it no longer appears in `update-user-role.tsx`, but I haven't seen the lint hook pass on the final files.

I used a plain `<select>` instead of the shared `Select`. The shared one is built around react-hook-form and only supports `defaultValue`, so it couldn't be controlled by the server value.
